newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus fisherman gets 15 months jail in AIDS case.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus fisherman gets 15 months jail in AIDS case.

text.p: Greek Cypriot fisherman Pavlos Georgiou was sentenced on Thursday to 15 months in jail for negligently giving the deadly virus that causes AIDS to his British lover, Janette Pink.
The decision, the first by a Cyprus court on a case of this kind, surprised local legal experts who were expecting a suspended sentence on Georgiou, 40.
"This case was so severe that even the maximum penalty as provided by law is evidently inadequate," Judge Antonis Liatsos told Georgiou, who is from the coastal holiday resort of Ayia Napa.
Under a decades-old law enacted to curtail cholera on the island, Georgiou faced a maximum sentence of two years in prison or a 1,500 Cyprus pound ($2,770) fine.
Liatsos said the 15-month sentence took into account that Georgiou, who has tested positive for the HIV virus that causes Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome, was dying.
"He is tragically condemned and it would be expected he would have tried to avoid putting others in the same condition...without telling her, he was ejaculating death in her for months," he said.
Georgiou, looking subdued, was immediately escorted from the court and into a police car to be taken to the central prisons in capital Nicosia.
Georgiou has not developed full-blown AIDS and shows no sign of suffering any disease. He is taking a triple drug regimen designed to delay onset of the disease.
Usually chatty with reporters, he sullenly refused to comment on the sentencing, pushing away microphones as two policemen held his upper arms.
He had a brief conversation with his twin brother, Petros, who was in the court.
"He has actually accepted it," the brother said of the sentence. We did not think he would go to jail. I have still got good feelings for Janette," he said.
The couple met in Petros's restaurant in late 1993.

Georgiou, a father of four who tested HIV positive in 1992, was found guilty of repeated sexual contact with Pink, 45, from Basildon, Essex, from January 1994 until she tested HIV positive in October 1994, without telling her of his condition.
Georgiou had denied the accusation, claiming Pink was well aware of his condition before they had intercourse.
But he admitted to having unprotected sex with her once, when they were both drunk, and at Pink's urging.

The court, describing Pink as an impeccable witness, accepted her testimony in its entirety, including her claim that Georgiou even concealed from her the death of his wife from an AIDS-related illness in August 1994.
Georgiou had told her his wife had leukaemia.
Liatsos dismissed submissions by defence lawyer Tassos Economou that Georgiou's cooperation with police was a mitigating factor.
"He tried to conceal his guilt all along," Liatsos said. "Taking into account the severity of the offence committed, I have no hesitation in stating that a prison sentence is unavoidable."
It was not immediately known whether Georgiou would appeal, but his lawyer said the evidence given during the trial was flawed.
"We will look at the issue again. There are people who did not come forward (at the trial) and they should not be able to sleep tonight," the lawyer said.
"I feel so sad because of the kids," said Petros. "I told him I will look after them. They are my responsibility."
Pavlos's youngest child, aged four, is HIV positive.
($1 = 0.540 Cyprus Pounds)
